documents.title: Amazon and the Hidden Cost of Reduced Competition

meta.subtitle: A case on market power after a major rival leaves
meta.summary: Amazon can look strongly consumer-friendly because it offers low prices, fast delivery, and convenience.
meta.centralQuestion: How can a reduction in competitive constraints change Amazon's strategic flexibility and consumer outcomes?

hero.alt: Visitors observe robotics and fulfillment operations inside Amazon's West Kaiserslautern fulfillment center.
hero.caption: Inside Amazon's West Kaiserslautern fulfillment center, May 2025.

blocks.heading: Business Context
blocks.body: Amazon is not only a retailer. It is also a marketplace, logistics system, advertising business, subscription ecosystem, and default starting point for many online searches.

blocks.title: Amazon links demand, supply, and fulfillment
blocks.note: The same system that lowers friction can also deepen dependence on the platform.

blocks.alt: A former Toys R Us store in Monroe, Louisiana, photographed after its closure.
blocks.caption: A documentary trace of the retailer’s physical exit.

blocks.title: Pricing after a major rival exits
blocks.finding: Amazon toy prices increased approximately 4% after Toys R Us exited the U.S. market.
blocks.comparison: The study compares the U.S. market with Canada.
blocks.caveat: A pricing pattern is not proof of every causal mechanism.

blocks.title: How weaker competition can change consumer outcomes
The case for convenience
blocks.body: Low prices, selection, delivery speed, and scale can all be explained by efficiency as well as power.

blocks.title: What this case does not establish
items: A result across every Amazon business

blocks.title: Understory Insight
blocks.statement: Convenience and competition can coexist, but convenience alone does not tell us how much constraint remains.

blocks.question: If convenience depends on competition, what should we watch when competition disappears?
